DEBIT-test values around the reported ones

Source: R/debit-map-seq.R
debit_map_seq.Rd

debit_map_seq() varies the reported means, standard deviations, and sample sizes a few steps up and down and DEBIT-tests each resulting value set. This shows whether a small error in reporting or computing could explain an inconsistency.

Call audit() on the output for summary statistics.

Usage

debit_map_seq(
  data,
  digits_x,
  digits_sd,
  x = NULL,
  sd = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  ...,
  data_type,
  sd_meaning = c("sd_sample", "sd_pop", "sd_sample_or_pop", "se"),
  formula = c("exact", "mean_n"),
  rounding = "up_or_down",
  threshold = 5,
  symmetric = FALSE,
  show_rec = FALSE,
  var = c("x", "sd", "n"),
  dispersion = 1:5,
  out_min = "auto",
  out_max = "auto",
  include_reported = FALSE,
  include_consistent = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame that debit_map() could take.

digits_x, digits_sd

Integer. The number of decimal places in x and sd, including trailing zeros. There are no defaults, since a numeric value does not keep them (1.40 is 1.4). Either a single number for the whole column or one number per row of data. If left out, they are taken from digits_x and digits_sd columns of data. They also set the step sizes for dispersing x and sd.

x, sd, n

Optionally, the names of the columns in data that contain these values, if they differ from the defaults.

...

These dots must be empty. Every argument after them must be named in full.

data_type

String. As in debit(). Give it as an argument or as a column of data; there is no default. It is returned as a column.

formula, rounding, threshold, symmetric, sd_meaning

Passed on to debit(), which explains the defaults.

show_rec

Logical. If TRUE, the reconstructed values are returned as further columns; see Value in debit_map(). Default is FALSE.

var

String. The variables to disperse. Default is c("x", "sd", "n").

dispersion

Numeric. Steps up and down from the reported values, in units of the last decimal place. Default is 1:5.

out_min, out_max

Limits on the dispersed values. Both default to "auto", which keeps n at 2 or above (1 under sd_meaning = "sd_pop" or "sd_sample_or_pop") and x and sd between 0 and 1. A number applies to every dispersed variable, and NULL removes the limit.

include_reported

Logical. Should the reported values themselves be part of the sequences? Default is FALSE.

include_consistent

Logical. Should consistent value sets be dispersed as well, not just inconsistent ones? Default is FALSE.

Value

A tibble with the columns of debit_map() output plus diff_var, case, and var, as in grim_map_seq(). As there, the other columns of data are dropped.

Summaries with audit()

audit() on debit_map_seq() output returns a tibble with one row per case and these columns:

  • x, sd, and n: the reported values, with data_type and their consistency.

  • hits_total: the number of DEBIT-consistent value sets found within the dispersion range.

  • hits_x, hits_sd, hits_n: the number found by varying x, sd, and n, respectively. If both include_reported and include_consistent are TRUE, a consistent reported value set is counted as well: once per variable here, and once in hits_total.

  • diff_x: the distance from x to the nearest consistent dispersed value, in dispersion steps. diff_x_up and diff_x_down are the signed steps to the nearest consistent value above and below (_down is negative).

  • diff_sd, diff_sd_up, diff_sd_down: the same for sd.

  • diff_n, diff_n_up, diff_n_down: the same for n.

A count or distance is NA if it depends on a dispersed value set whose consistency is NA, on a variable whose reported value is missing, which is not dispersed, or on rows removed from the output, as by filter().

Call audit() again on that summary to summarize these columns further. na_count and na_rate there count the cases without a consistent value within the dispersion range, and those that a missing value leaves unknown.

Examples

# `debit_map_seq()` takes the same input as `debit_map()`:
pigs3
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>       x    sd     n
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  0.53  0.5   1683
#> 2  0.44  0.5   1683
#> 3  0.77  0.42  1683
#> 4  0.19  0.35  1683
#> 5  0.34  0.47  1683
#> 6  0.93  0.25  1683
#> 7  0.12  0.33  1683

out <- pigs3 |>
  dplyr::slice(3:4) |>
  debit_map_seq(digits_x = 2, digits_sd = 2, data_type = "integer")
out
#> # A tibble: 30 × 10
#> # DEBIT: default settings
#>        x    sd     n data_type digits_x digits_sd consistency diff_var  case
#>    <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>        <int>     <int> <lgl>          <int> <int>
#>  1  0.14  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 TRUE              -5     2
#>  2  0.15  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 TRUE              -4     2
#>  3  0.16  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE             -3     2
#>  4  0.17  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE             -2     2
#>  5  0.18  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE             -1     2
#>  6  0.2   0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE              1     2
#>  7  0.21  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE              2     2
#>  8  0.22  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE              3     2
#>  9  0.23  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE              4     2
#> 10  0.24  0.35  1683 integer          2         2 FALSE              5     2
#> # ℹ 20 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: var <chr>

# Case-wise summaries:
out |>
  audit()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 18
#>       x    sd     n data_type consistency hits_total hits_x hits_sd hits_n
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <chr>     <lgl>            <int>  <int>   <int>  <int>
#> 1  0.19  0.35  1683 integer   FALSE                4      2       2      0
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: diff_x <int>, diff_x_up <int>, diff_x_down <int>,
#> #   diff_sd <int>, diff_sd_up <int>, diff_sd_down <int>, diff_n <int>,
#> #   diff_n_up <int>, diff_n_down <int>
